definition: Artificial wisdom (AW) is an artificial intelligence (AI) system which is able to display the human traits of wisdom and morals while being able to contemplate its own “endpoint”.
details: Artificial wisdom can be described as artificial intelligence reaching the top-level of decision-making when confronted with the most complex challenging situations. The term artificial wisdom is used when the "intelligence" is based on more than by chance collecting and interpreting data, but by design enriched with smart and conscience strategies that wise people would use.

explainer.lead: Artificial wisdom is a proposed level of AI that goes beyond collecting data and making intelligent decisions. The idea is that a system should also show wisdom and morals in very difficult situations, while reflecting on its own endpoint.

tiers.eli5: Instead of just being clever at answering questions, it would be the kind of helper that also knows what is right and wrong, and can even think about when its own job should end.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers frame it as enrichment by design with smart, conscience-driven strategies rather than chance data collection. The pitfall is that wisdom and conscience cannot be collected by chance from data alone, so the design must supply them deliberately.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, an AW system displays the human traits of wisdom and morals while being able to contemplate its own endpoint, operating at the top level of decision-making for the most complex, challenging situations. Its stated limit is that the intelligence must come from designed strategies, not from chance collection and interpretation of data.

explainer.example: A hypothetical disaster-response system must distribute a limited supply of medicine among several shelters. Rather than choosing only the fastest delivery plan, it considers need, fairness, and possible harm, then explains its allocation while reflecting on whether continuing toward its assigned endpoint remains appropriate.
explainer.intuition: Being intelligent means finding effective answers; being wise also means handling difficult choices with moral judgment. Artificial wisdom adds the further idea that the system can reflect on its own endpoint.
howItWorks: Gather and interpret information about a complex situation.
Consider possible decisions instead of relying on chance pattern collection alone.
Apply deliberate strategies associated with wise and conscientious judgment.
Weigh the moral character of the decision alongside its practical result.
Reflect on the system's own endpoint as part of its highest-level decision-making.
explainer.whyItMatters: The concept asks whether advanced AI should be judged only by capability or also by the quality and morality of its hardest decisions. It places purpose and self-reflection alongside data-driven performance.
misconceptions: It is not simply AI with more data, greater accuracy, or faster decisions.
It is not a particular neural network design or training method.
Producing convincing statements about morality does not by itself establish artificial wisdom.
